findings.description: The ProviderContextLimitError arm shrinks max_tokens and `continue`s, which consumes one iteration of `for attempt in range(max_retries + 1)`. When the context-limit error arrives on the final iteration (or `retry.max_retries` is 0, so range(1)), `continue` ends the loop and control falls through to the post-loop RetriesExhaustedError. `last_typed_error` is never assigned in this arm, so the exhausted error carries no ProviderContextLimitError. cheval's RetriesExhaustedError arm walks the chain, so the identical payload is dispatched to the next voice, exactly what D-1.1b forbids, and `_calibration_needed_exit` never runs so nothing is appended to .run/ceiling-observed.json.
findings.failure_mode: Operator sets retry.max_retries: 0 (or earlier attempts hit 429/5xx and the provider's prompt-too-long 400 lands on the last attempt). Result: RetriesExhaustedError → chain walk with the same oversized payload → second provider call fails the same way → CHAIN_EXHAUSTED, no observed-bound record, no calibration_needed envelope.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not spend an attempt on the shrink: track `shrink_pending` and loop with a while/extra iteration, or when `attempt == max_retries` set `last_typed_error = e` and `raise` instead of `continue`. In all cases assign `last_typed_error = e` before `continue` so a fall-through RetriesExhaustedError carries the typed cause, and have cheval's RetriesExhaustedError arm check for a ProviderContextLimitError cause and route to `_calibration_needed_exit`.

findings.description: `_ceiling_unverified` is computed once from the HEAD entry's pre-flight GateOutcome (line ~1843) but consulted on every hop of the walk, and the RateLimitError arm short-circuits on it unconditionally (no check that the 429 is the token-limit class). Two consequences: (a) a plain requests-per-minute 429 on the head while above its probed bound ends the invocation as RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED instead of walking; (b) after a walkable head failure, a 429 or ProviderContextLimitError on a CALIBRATED fallback is still classed as RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED / CEILING_UNVERIFIED_LIMIT (line 2256) and recorded against the fallback model. The supplied test file test_ceiling_e2e.py contradicts this code directly: `test_request_rate_429_while_unverified_walks_to_the_next_hop` expects `RateLimitError("anthropic")` to walk with no calibration row, and `test_unverified_status_is_per_hop_not_inherited_from_the_head` expects PROVIDER_OUTAGE x2 and PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT on the calibrated fallback. Both fail against the diff as written.
findings.failure_mode: Operator opts in (LOA_CHEVAL_UNCALIBRATED_CEILING=derived), head gets an ordinary rate-limit 429 → exit RATE_LIMITED, no fallback tried, a spurious RATE_LIMIT_UNVERIFIED row appended to the observed store. Or: head 503s, calibrated fallback 429s → terminal exit instead of walk, calibration_needed emitted for a model that was never unverified.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the short-circuit on `getattr(_e, 'token_limited', False) and _hop_unverified`, where `_hop_unverified` is recomputed per hop (e.g. `_ceiling_unverified` only for `_idx == 0`, or compute `input_bound(...)` for the hop entry and compare `_walk_estimate` to its probed/calibrated value). Use the same per-hop flag for the CEILING_UNVERIFIED_LIMIT vs PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT classification at line 2256.

findings.description: `_calibration_needed_exit` stores the raw provider error text: `"message_redacted": str(_exc)` into `models_failed` and `f"{_exc} — not walked..."` into the stderr `_error_json`. No redaction helper is applied even though the field is named `message_redacted`. Provider 400 bodies echo request fragments; the supplied test `test_calibration_exit_redacts_secret_shapes_in_the_recorded_message` (which patches the modelinv-layer `redact_payload_strings` to identity, so it requires cheval-side redaction) asserts the `sk-ant-api03-...` token must not appear in `message_redacted` or stderr. The diff code leaks it in both.
findings.failure_mode: A provider error body containing a key-shaped string (echoed prompt content, proxy-injected header text) is written verbatim to the MODELINV envelope / model-invoke.jsonl and to the operator's stderr log, persisting a secret in audit storage.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `str(_exc)` through the existing redaction helper used by the other `models_failed` arms (the same redact used for `message_redacted` elsewhere in cmd_invoke) before placing it in `_modelinv_state` and before formatting the `_error_json` message.

findings.description: The per-hop I1 fit (line 2089) uses `_walk_estimate`, which the pre-flight replaces with the provider's count_tokens value when available. The fitted `_hop_budget` is then passed as `max_tokens=` to `_lookup_max_input_tokens`, whose policy bound is `min(..., context_window - max_tokens)` (asserted by `test_i1_and_i2_per_entry_from_the_fields`). After a shrink, `context_window - _hop_budget == counted estimate`. But the walk gate immediately below still computes `estimate_tokens(messages)` (the chars/3.5 heuristic) and compares it against that bound. Whenever the provider count is lower than the heuristic (typical for English prose, where the heuristic over-counts by ~10-15 %), heuristic > bound and the hop is skipped as ROUTING_MISS even though the provider said it fits.
findings.failure_mode: 170K-counted prompt on a 200K entry with an Anthropic head: pre-flight count = 170K, fit shrinks max_tokens to 30K, walk gate bound = 170K, heuristic estimate = ~190K → ROUTING_MISS on every anthropic hop → CHAIN_EXHAUSTED for a request the provider count certified as fitting. (Not caught by test_170k_on_a_200k_entry because its MagicMock adapter yields no int count.)
findings.suggested_fix: Make the walk gate compare `_walk_estimate` (the authoritative estimate after pre-flight) instead of re-running `estimate_tokens(messages)`, or compute the walk gate's I1 bound from the UNfitted budget and only apply the fit afterwards. Add an e2e test with a `count_tokens` returning less than the heuristic.

findings.description: The long-context threshold test uses `input_tokens > threshold`, where `input_tokens` is Anthropic's `usage.input_tokens`, which (per the ledger docstring, cycle-124 FR-4) EXCLUDES cache_read and cache_creation tokens. Anthropic's published premium rule applies when the total prompt (uncached + cache-read + cache-write) exceeds 200K. A 60K-fresh / 150K-cache-read request is billed premium by the provider but at base rate by this ledger, and `long_context` is not set, so cost-report's long_context_rows undercounts.
findings.failure_mode: Systematic under-reporting of spend for prompt-caching heavy workloads above 200K total context; daily budget enforcement (BudgetEnforcer) lets more through than the real bill.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_creation_tokens > threshold` (mirroring the provider's definition) and document the rule in the PricingEntry comment.

findings.description: `_obs` falls back to `int(_walk_estimate or 0)` when the provider message states no `input_tokens`. That happens for a 413 (byte-size verdict, not a token verdict) and for any 400 matched by the broad `is_context_limit_message` markers ("context window", "input length"), and `_walk_estimate` is None when LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_INPUT_GATE is set. The heuristic estimate or 0 is then persisted as `observed_input_tokens` with a bound-lowering error_class (PROVIDER_CONTEXT_LIMIT), so the observed store can be poisoned by a non-token error, and a 0 observation may clamp the entry's bound to nothing until the operator runs the probe.
findings.failure_mode: A 413 from a proxy's request-body-size limit (or a misclassified 400) records observed_input_tokens=heuristic/0 for the entry; every subsequent call to that model is pre-empted CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE until .run/ceiling-observed.json is cleared or the entry is recalibrated.
findings.suggested_fix: Only lower the bound when the provider stated `input_tokens`/`limit`; when neither is parseable, record the row with `observed_input_tokens=None` and an error_class that does not lower (or skip the record), and never record 0. Treat 413 separately from the prompt-too-long 400 class.

findings.cross_file_justification: The default of `CompletionRequest.temperature` changed from 0.7 to None in types.py (in diff); only anthropic, bedrock, google and openai adapters were updated to call `wire_temperature`. Any other adapter or CLI/headless transport that reads `request.temperature` directly is outside the diff but now receives None.
findings.description: `temperature` is now Optional and None by default, and cheval.py passes `binding.temperature` (often None). The four adapters in the diff route through `wire_temperature`, but any provider adapter, CLI/headless adapter argv builder, or mock-fixture matcher not in this diff that does `body["temperature"] = request.temperature` or `str(request.temperature)` will emit `null`/`None` on the wire and get a 400 or a malformed CLI flag.
findings.failure_mode: A non-updated adapter (e.g. an OpenAI-compatible or headless CLI path) sends `"temperature": null` → provider 400 on every call under the new default, surfacing as a chain walk / INVALID_INPUT.
findings.suggested_fix: grep for `request.temperature` / `.temperature` across loa_cheval/providers and the cli/headless adapters; route every wire write through `wire_temperature`. Add a transport-matrix test asserting no adapter body contains `temperature: null`.
